title: ABA opening statement to the Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
headline: ABA Joint Select Committee opening statement on AI in banking
summary: The Australian Banking Association presented its opening statement to the Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, outlining banks' current use of AI for fraud detection, customer service, and real-time payment monitoring. The ABA noted that existing technology-neutral regulation overseen by APRA and ASIC currently governs banking AI without requiring new AI-specific rules. However, the submission warned that offshore criminals are deploying AI for large-scale fraud, requiring banks to utilise AI defensively while advocating for exemptions from transparency obligations that could compromise security.
why_it_matters: Banks and regulated financial entities must balance AI transparency mandates with the operational necessity of protecting fraud and scam-detection models from reverse-engineering by bad actors.

quotes.text: Australia’s banks are not approaching artificial intelligence as a distant prospect. It is already at work in our industry, every hour of every day.
Transparency obligations should not require us to reveal how those systems work, because that simply hands criminals a blueprint.

classification.significance_reason: Outlines the Australian banking sector's official stance on AI regulation, APRA/ASIC oversight, and the tension between AI transparency and scam detection.
